newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ACCC issues rules over telecom access.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ACCC issues rules over telecom access.

text.p: The Australian Commission and Consumer Commission (ACCC) on Monday issued a list of telecommunications services to which regulated access will be established from July 1 for carriers and service providers.

The ACCC, which will become the new industry regulator from Tuesday when the industry is fully deregulated, said as a result, service providers must be provided with these services on request from any carriers or carriage service providers.
"This will allow service providers and new entrants to have access to similar services as are now being obtained by Optus and Vodafone from Telstra," ACCC said.

State-owned Telstra Corp Ltd operates Australia's main telephone network, while Optus Communications Pty Ltd and Vodafone Plc were allowed to operate as carriers under partial deregulation of the industry in 1992.
ACCC said the new access regime is for both voice and data services.

It said in keeping with the government's intention to remove the exemption of pay TV carriage from the access regime, the ACCC also has deemed a carriage service for the provision of broadcasting services on cable networks.
ACCC said this would provide opportunities for content providers to access pay TV networks.

The commission said it had chosen not to deem transmission links between capital cities. "Such transmission services are potentially contestable in the new environment where new carriers will be able to install their own facilities," it said.
It said regulated access which could involve the ACCC setting prices may distort competition developing and undermine incentives for efficient investment in transmission facilities.
Under the new era of deregulation, there is no limit to the number of carriers to be allowed in the local market.
